findings.summary: The required direct-publisher absent-baseline test reaches the internal ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync through a name-based reflection helper, so the coverage is correct but coupled to the method's exact name and signature.
findings.detail: The test assembly has no InternalsVisibleTo and the production boundary must stay internal (ADR-024 clause 2), so the worker added a test-local `RestoreAsync(ArtworkPublisher, ArtworkLifecycleFence)` helper that resolves `typeof(ArtworkPublisher).GetMethod("RestoreAsync", BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic)` and invokes it on the same instance with the same arguments. `Assert.NotNull(method)` prevents a silent no-op if the method disappears, and reflection over non-public members is already an established pattern in this test project (for example EnhancedCoexistenceTests.cs:240, ConfigurationRoundTripTests.cs:153). The cost is that a rename or an added overload becomes a runtime failure (or an AmbiguousMatchException) rather than a compile error; the assertions themselves are unaffected. This is a test-only mechanism and no production visibility was widened.

src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkPublisher.cs:510-514 (single internal RestoreAsync overload; internal boundary unchanged)

findings.summary: The crash-recoverability case models the restart by reconstructing the services over the same state root, not by killing and restarting a process; the limitation is stated honestly and the reconstruction is genuine.
findings.detail: CoordinatorDrivenRestorationIsResumedByTheOrdinaryRecoveryGate interrupts the save with an injected InvalidOperationException thrown from the fake host before any bytes are applied. Inspection of the production path confirms this is the only way the durable state can be left behind: ExecuteRestorationAsync has already written the RestorePending state and the Prepared/MutationStarted Restoration operation, and the exception is not an OperationCanceledException, so it escapes ExecuteRestorationAsync and RestoreCoreAsync and is contained by RestoreAsync's bounded catch, which persists nothing further (src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkPublisher.cs:725-734, 547-552). The test then builds a fresh StateRepository, SourceArtifactStore, PublishedArtworkStateStore, ArtworkOperationStore, ArtworkPublisher and ArtworkReconciler over the same root; the stores read from disk on every Read (src/ArrTags/State/StateRepository.cs:58-64, src/ArrTags/Artwork/PublishedArtworkStateStore.cs:66-70), so nothing of the interrupted attempt is carried in memory. The resumed reconcile is a real decision-table pass: the operation is non-terminal, LastOperationId does not match, the observed image matches neither ObservedAfter nor CandidateAfter, and ExpectedBeforeIdentity still compares Owned, which yields ArtworkRecoveryAction.Resume and the restoration branch of ResumeRecoveryAsync. The assertions go beyond `OperationId != null` (which TQR-20.1-02 flagged as insufficient): they assert the durable Kind=Restoration, LifecycleFence=Normal, IsTerminal=false, State=RestorePending, zero completed mutations before the restart, and after the restart Completed/IsCommitted, the same OperationId, exactly one save of the retained baseline, and state Restored. The worker states plainly that this is not a real process restart.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArtworkReconcilerTests.cs (CoordinatorDrivenRestorationIsResumedByTheOrdinaryRecoveryGate, fresh services over the same root)

src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkPublisher.cs:640-665 (state and operation written before the mutation), :725-734 (only OperationCanceledException is caught at the mutation), :547-552 (bounded outer catch writes nothing), :1266-1271 (restoration branch of ResumeRecoveryAsync)
src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkRecoveryDecisions.cs:44-100 (Resume requires a non-terminal operation, no durable final state, and an owned before-identity match)
src/ArrTags/State/StateRepository.cs:58-64 and src/ArrTags/Artwork/PublishedArtworkStateStore.cs:66-70 (every read hits disk; no in-memory cache)
findings.recommended_action: None. Keep the wording honest: the case proves durable-record recoverability through the ordinary recovery gate, not process-level restart survival; a real process-kill leg belongs to live pinned-host verification in Phase 21.

findings.summary: The genuine non-empty NoFittingBadge coordinator case is ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT-guarded and therefore absent from the default suite; the guard is a real environment requirement, the skip is reported, and I confirmed 1/1 under the pinned native oracle.
findings.detail: NonFittingSelectionOnAnOwnedSessionPassesThroughAsNoFittingBadgeWithoutMutation is [SkiaNativeFact], which sets Skip unless ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 (tests/ArrTags.Tests/SkiaHostCompatibilityTests.cs:142-153). The guard is honest: the case constructs a real SkiaBadgeRenderer and encodes/decodes an SKBitmap through RendererBehaviorFixtures.CreateOpaquePng(10, 10), which cannot run without the pinned native runtime, exactly like the pre-existing decode-dependent siblings. I ran it in the default configuration (reported as an explicit [SKIP] line, 1 skip) and under the repository's pinned probe sysroot with ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 (Failed 0, Passed 1, Skipped 0, Total 1), so the case genuinely executes there. The selection it uses is real and non-empty: the coordinator Request() supplies RenderTestFixtures.BuildMetadata() with quality, resolution, codec and source values, and at 10x10 the layout engine cannot fit any pill, which is the same deterministic construction the 20.1 renderer-level case uses. In the default configuration the NoFittingBadge preserve guarantee therefore rests on the 20.1 FakeRenderer theory row, which does run; the native case closes TQR-20.1-03's single-configuration request for the native configuration. No ADR-024 behavior is claimed verified by the default suite on the strength of the skip alone.

acceptance_criteria_reviewed.criterion: 1. Direct publisher absent-baseline removal (explicit Phase 20 acceptance criterion)
acceptance_criteria_reviewed.evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArtworkPublisherTests.cs AbsentBaselineRestorationRemovesTheArrtagsImageWithoutSaveOrUpdate builds a synthetic persisted Published state through the new PublishedState(active, sourceBytes: null) helper (CaptureSession with an Absent source identity and no artifact, then CommitPublication whose active identity matches what the fake host reports so the ownership revalidation is Owned), then calls the internal RestoreAsync(..., Normal, ...) directly. It asserts Completed + IsCommitted, RemoveCalls==1, SaveCalls==0, UpdateCalls==0, SavedBytes/SavedContentType null, host CurrentBytes null (the fake's RemoveImageAsync nulls it, so a removal is not invisible), PhaseAtRemove == MutationStarted (write-ahead before the mutation), the durable operation Kind=Restoration / Phase=Committed / CandidateAfterPresence=Absent / CandidateAfterContentSha256 null / SourceArtifactId null / LifecycleFence=Normal / matching OperationId, and the state Restored with SourcePresence=Absent and both identities released. The removal boundary is therefore proven and no save or item update can be hiding. Independent sensitivity: with the production removal branch replaced by an unconditional SaveImageAsync in a throwaway copy of the tree (/tmp/20.2/probe), the test fails (Expected Completed, Actual RecoveryBlocked), so it cannot pass for the wrong reason. The test's own comment correctly records that the coordinator cannot reach this branch.

Owned empty selection restoring the retained baseline is 20.1's EmptySelectionOnAnOwnedSessionRestoresTheRetainedBaseline, now strengthened with RemoveCalls==0 and the durable operation's Kind=Restoration / Phase=Committed / LifecycleFence=Normal / OperationId. The non-owned empty selection stays a pass-through (20.1, with ReconciliationOutcome null as the isolating assertion, now also annotated in the diff). The five other reasons keep the 20.1 theory (NoMetadata, NoFittingBadge, IneligibleSurface, MatchNotEligible, SourceUnavailable) with unchanged save/update/remove counts and a retained Published state. The one genuinely new leg is the native NoFittingBadge case using a real SkiaBadgeRenderer and a non-empty resolved selection that cannot fit on a 10x10 baseline; it is honestly native-guarded, skips in the default suite, and passes 1/1 under the pinned oracle.

Permitted: EmptySelectionRestorationIsPermittedUnderDisableAndUninstallFences (coordinator, theory Disable/Uninstall, asserts Restored/Completed, the retained baseline written, RemoveCalls==0, and a committed Restoration operation carrying the active fence) and RestorationIsPermittedUnderDisableAndUninstallFences (publisher, theory, same fence on the operation). Refused with no mutation: NonRestorableFencePreservesAnOwnedSessionWithoutMutation (20.1, ItemRemoved via the coordinator) and the new publisher second layer RestorationIsRefusedUnderTheItemRemovedFenceWithoutMutation (NothingToReconcile, zero save/update/remove, host bytes unchanged, Published state kept, no operation record). Invalid/unreadable fence record: InvalidFenceRecordPreservesAnOwnedSessionWithoutMutation writes a corrupt authoritative fence record so ArtworkLifecycleFenceStore.Read returns ArtworkLifecycleFenceState.Invalid (IsValid=false, Fence=Uninstall) and asserts pass-through, ReconciliationOutcome null, no mutation, retained Published state, and that only the original Publication operation exists. Independent sensitivity: dropping IsValid from the coordinator guard made exactly this test fail (Expected RenderPassThrough, Actual Restored) while the 20.1 ItemRemoved case still passed, so the new case isolates the fail-closed guard and the publisher-layer case isolates the second layer. The worker's interpretation that an 'invalid record' can only be observed at the store read is correct.

acceptance_criteria_reviewed.criterion: 4. Crash recoverability through the ordinary recovery gate
acceptance_criteria_reviewed.evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArtworkReconcilerTests.cs CoordinatorDrivenRestorationIsResumedByTheOrdinaryRecoveryGate: a Normal-fence coordinator (no fence store) drives the empty-selection restoration, the injected save failure leaves RestorePending plus a non-terminal Restoration operation with zero completed mutations, and fresh stores/publisher/reconciler over the same root resume it through ArtworkRecoveryDecisions -> ArtworkReconciler.ReconcileAsync -> ExecuteRecoveryAsync -> ResumeRecoveryAsync -> ResumeRestorationAsync to Completed/Committed with the same OperationId and exactly one save of the retained baseline. The seeded state uses a helper whose active identity matches the fake host's reported bytes so the resume passes the ownership revalidation. Independent sensitivity: changing the restoration branch condition in ResumeRecoveryAsync to ArtworkOperationKind.Publication made the test fail (Expected Completed, Actual RecoveryBlocked). This closes the TQR-20.1-02 gap that OperationId != null does not establish recoverability.

tests/ArrTags.Tests/ArtworkGenerationResultTests.cs (new file) covers Completed->Restored, Cancelled->Cancelled, NothingToReconcile->RenderPassThrough, and OwnershipLost/OwnershipUnknown/RecoveryBlocked->Blocked, asserting ReconciliationOutcome, the retained NoDisplayableValue pass-through reason, the reason text, the OperationId, a null state, and Preserved false only for the completed mapping; plus the committed-state identity case, the refused-restoration classification, and the null-reconciliation guard. The mapping asserted matches ArtworkGenerationResult.FromRestoration exactly, and the test does not restate the implementation as a tautology only: it pins the retained pass-through reason and the Preserved contract, which are the caller-visible guarantees.

MissingFenceStoreDrivesTheRestoreUnderTheNormalFence builds ArtworkGenerationCoordinator without the fences argument after a real publication and asserts Restored/Completed, the retained baseline written, and a committed Restoration operation with LifecycleFence=Normal. Independent sensitivity: changing the coordinator's null default to ArtworkLifecycleFenceState.Invalid failed this test (Expected Restored, Actual RenderPassThrough) while the fence-store-backed 20.1 restore case still passed, so the case isolates the null default and closes TQR-20.1-01.
